newsitem.title: POLAND: DOMESTIC DEMAND DRIVES POLISH ECONOMY - STATOFFICE.
newsitem.headline: DOMESTIC DEMAND DRIVES POLISH ECONOMY - STATOFFICE.

text.p: The growth of the Polish economy in the first three quarters of 1996 was mainly driven by domestic consumption and investment, the head of the Central Statistic Office (GUS) said on Wednesday.
"The main engine of the economy in the first three quarters of 1996 was domestic demand for consumption and investments... and not exports," Roman Sawinski told a news conference.
Sawinski said growth rates for exports have been slowing while imports have been thriving this year.

According to current account figures, exports grew by six percent in the first eight months of this year while imports rose by over 30 percent, which increased the trade gap to nearly $4.5 billion from $710 million in the same period of 1995.

GUS said the continued quick growth of industrial output, at 8.0 percent year-on-year in September, was the result of high investment activity and increases in real incomes of most households in Poland.

During the January-August period, investment in Polish firms grew by 25 percent from the same period of last year and reached 20.5 billion zlotys. GUS said investment in the private sector increased by 63 percent from the same period of 1995.
Sawinski said real wages grew by 4.6 percent over the first three quarters of the year.
